finderFindings.claim: The new SRU filter compares against a hard-coded 'SRU' string when `SGroup.isSRUSGroup` already does this check.
finderFindings.scenario: New line: `.filter((sgroup) => sgroup !== sG && sgroup.type === 'SRU')`. The existing helper is `static isSRUSGroup(sGroup: SGroup): boolean { return sGroup.type === this.TYPES.SRU; }` at sgroup.ts:923, and InfoPanel.tsx already uses it. If the SRU type identifier or the polymer check changes in `SGroup.isSRUSGroup` / `SGroup.TYPES.SRU`, this filter keeps the old string. Star atoms shared with another polymer would then turn back into carbons. Use `.filter((sgroup) => sgroup !== sG && SGroup.isSRUSGroup(sgroup))`.

finderFindings.claim: The new test adds `as unknown as` casts for RenderOptions and HTMLElement instead of using correctly typed stubs.
finderFindings.scenario: The new test repeats the Render/ReStruct setup from atomMerge.test.ts:55-61 and adds two more casts: `} as unknown as RenderOptions;` and `new Render(document as unknown as HTMLElement, options)`. Both are double casts that switch off type checking. If Render later reads a RenderOptions field that this three-field stub lacks, the test still compiles and fails only at runtime. R5 covers unit tests too. Fix it with one typed setup helper, like `createRestruct` in sgroup.test.ts:58, typed through a correct partial or factory instead of a cast. Both tests can then share it, so the casts are not copied again.

confirmed.claim: The new test adds `as unknown as` casts for RenderOptions and HTMLElement instead of using correctly typed stubs.
confirmed.scenario: The new test copies the Render/ReStruct setup from atomMerge.test.ts:55-61, so it adds two new casts: `} as unknown as RenderOptions;` (line 137) and `new Render(document as unknown as HTMLElement, options)` (line 138). Both turn off type checking. If Render later reads a RenderOptions field that this three-field stub does not have, the test still compiles and fails only at runtime. `createRestruct` in sgroup.test.ts:58 does the same setup but uses the same casts, so it is not a cast-free model. The fix is one shared, correctly typed setup helper (a full RenderOptions factory or a typed partial merged with defaults) that both test files use instead of repeating the casts.

confirmed.claim: The new SRU filter compares against a hard-coded 'SRU' string when `SGroup.isSRUSGroup` already does this check.
confirmed.scenario: The new filter that collects the end atoms of other SRU polymers checks the hard-coded string 'SRU'. It does not call the existing `SGroup.isSRUSGroup(sgroup)` helper (`return sGroup.type === this.TYPES.SRU;`), which InfoPanel.tsx:138 already uses. `SGroup` is already imported in this file, so the helper can be used with no new dependency: `.filter((sgroup) => sgroup !== sG && SGroup.isSRUSGroup(sgroup))`. Today the behavior is the same. The duplicated type check is what R9 forbids.
